title: The guard validates the key that names the class, and the factory instantiates from a different key
index_line: T-0092 · CODE_EXEC · Yii behaviour attach: guard checks `class` is a Behaviour, factory reads `__class` → arbitrary instantiation · php · corroborated
invariant_violated: The behaviour-attachment guard assumed the type being instantiated is named by the key it validates. The configuration array can name a type twice — `class` and `__class` — and the factory reads the other one, so a value that passes the allowlist is not the value that gets constructed.

mechanism.does: a request body carries a component configuration containing an 'as <name>' key
the framework's __set detects the 'as ' prefix and calls attachBehavior with the attacker-supplied array
the guard verifies that $value['class'] is a subclass of the Behaviour base class
the instantiation path resolves a different key ('__class'), so the validated class is never the class that is constructed
the factory instantiates the attacker-named class with '__construct()' arguments taken from the same array
the constructed gadget runs (e.g. FnStream with an attacker callback, PhpManager pointed at a session file), yielding arbitrary code execution

source.http.body.value: a JSON/PHP-array request body whose nested config contains 'as <name>' with class/__class/__construct() keys

gadget.magic-method.value: the gadget chain: magic methods and destructors reached through the attacker-chosen class

guard.sandbox.value: the 'class must be a Behaviour subclass' allowlist that validates one key while the factory reads another

encoding.object-stream.value: the configuration array itself is the object-instantiation encoding — no serialized stream needed

preconditions.expr: the application builds component/config arrays from request data (mass assignment of 'as ' keys)
the installed yii2 version is 2.0.52+ unaffected / below 2.0.52 affected

check.spec: grep -r '"yiisoft/yii2"' composer.lock 2>/dev/null | head -3; grep -r 'VERSION' vendor/yiisoft/yii2/BaseYii.php 2>/dev/null | head -3

preconditions.expr: a gadget class with a useful magic method or destructor is autoloadable

success: an object of a class unrelated to Behaviour is instantiated with attacker constructor arguments
a gadget side effect fires (outbound callback, file written or read at an attacker-chosen path)
failure_like: the config is rejected because '__class' is not an allowed key
the fix resolves the type from the validated key only
false_positive: a PHP error naming a class does not prove control — require the constructor arguments to be attacker-chosen and the side effect observed
behaviour attachment working as designed with a legitimate Behaviour subclass is not this bug

hazards: every framework with config-array instantiation (Yii, Laravel, Symfony, Spring, .NET type converters): two keys can name the type
allowlists that validate a sibling key rather than the value used downstream
no unserialize() needed — the config array is the object-injection encoding, so deserialization-only filters miss it
non_transfers: factories that take the type from the validated key or a fixed map
applications that never build component configs from request data

evidence.target: Yii 2 before 2.0.52, behaviour attachment via 'as <name>' config (CVE-2024-58136)

provenance.author: SensePost / Orange Cyberdefense CSIRT
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2024-58136 mechanism: the "as <name>" config key attaches a behaviour; the guard checks $value["class"] is a Behavior subclass, but the config also carries a "__class" key that the object factory uses, so an attacker instantiates an arbitrary class with attacker-chosen constructor arguments (Guzzle FnStream with _fn_close, yii\rbac\PhpManager with itemFile) — object injection to RCE

provenance.author: Yii Framework (release notice)
provenance.corroborates: vendor: the issue is the regression introduced in GHSA-cjcc-p67m-7qxm while attaching behaviour defined by the __class array key, fixed in 2.0.52 and tracked as CVE-2024-58136

provenance.author: MITRE / NIST NVD
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2024-58136 description (mishandles attaching behaviour defined by an __class array key; regression of CVE-2024-4990)
